title: Rafael Jodar makes ATP Rankings history as he secures huge milestone in standout season
article_text:
Rafael Jodar will make history next week after the Spaniard secured his debut inside the top 10 of the ATP Rankings.

The third seed at the Swiss Indoors in Basel this week, Jodar was beaten by Valentin Vacherot in the second round of the ATP 500 event.

However, with Vacherot going on to defeat Taylor Fritz in the semi-final of the event on Saturday, 20-year-old Jodar is now guaranteed to reach the top 10 of the ATP Rankings for the first time next week.

Currently ranked 11th in the world, the Spaniard is projected to rise one place to world No 10 — and will achieve something that no man in the history of the men’s game can match.

Jodar will become the first player since the ATP Rankings were introduced in 1973 to reach the top 10 during his first full season on tour, having only made his Grand Slam debut at the Australian Open in January, and his Masters 1000 debut at the Indian Wells Open in March.

The Spaniard will also become the player with the second shortest gap between his top 100 debut and his top 10 debut, with the 217 days between those two milestones only bettered by the 210 days between Boris Becker’s top 100 and top 10 debuts back in 1985.

Just 287 days separate the start of Jodar’s first full season and his top 10 debut, cementing a remarkable rise for the Spaniard who has become one of the most talked-about players in men’s tennis.

Jodar’s breakout season has been full of notable milestones, perhaps none more so than winning his first ATP Tour title at the Grand Prix Hassan II in Marrakesh this May.

The Spaniard defeated Marco Trungelliti to lift the first tour-level title of his career, a result that was followed by two more runner-up finishes at ATP level.

Jodar reached the first ATP 500 final of his career at the Citi Open in July, falling to Taylor Fritz in the championship match, while he reached the first Masters 1000 final of his career at the Shanghai Masters in October — falling in three tight sets to compatriot Alejandro Davidovich Fokina.

At Masters 1000 level, the Spaniard was also a semi-finalist on his tournament debut at the Canadian Open in August, while he was also a quarter-finalist at both the Madrid Open and Italian Open during the spring.

And, he also reached his first Grand Slam quarter-final in just his second major main draw appearance at Roland Garros.

Seeded 27th in Paris, it took second seed and eventual champion Alexander Zverev to stop him in the last eight, with Jodar also reaching the third round of Wimbledon just a few weeks later.

Following on from his second-round showing in Basel, Jodar will return to action at the Paris Masters next week.

The Spaniard is the ninth seed at the Masters 1000 tournament and will start his campaign in round one against Alejandro Tabilo, with a potential clash versus fifth seed Flavio Cobolli in the third round.

Jodar is among those battling for a place in the ATP Finals, with the 20-year-old knocked down to 10th place in the Race to Turin following Alex de Minaur’s run to the Vienna Open final.

title: Alexander Zverev’s Vienna Open prize money and ranking points after semi-final exit
article_text:
Alexander Zverev will claim the world No 1 ranking for the first time on Monday but will not have a new title to celebrate after defeat in the semi-final of the Vienna Open.

A runner-up at this tournament twelve months ago, Zverev was the top seed at the ATP 500 event this year and was among the favourites for glory in the Austrian capital.

However, his hopes of glory were dashed in a dramatic semi-final on Saturday, with the German tasting defeat to fifth seed Alex de Minaur.

After dropping the opening set to his Australian rival, Zverev rebounded with a dominant second set, but it was de Minaur who held firm in the closing stages to seal a 6-4, 1-6, 7-6(4) triumph — booking a date with Carlos Alcaraz in Sunday’s final.

Zverev will become the 30th world No 1 in ATP Rankings history on Monday despite his defeat but, with his campaign now over, we look at the ranking points and prize money he will take home from the event.

Significant ranking points are on offer in Vienna, with the winner of Sunday’s final between de Minaur and Alcaraz set to earn 500 ranking points, while the runner-up will take home 330 points.

Zverev earned 330 points for his runner-up finish twelve months, with 320 of those points dropping off the ATP Rankings at the start of this week.

For his semi-final run in Vienna this year, the German has earned 200 ranking points.

With the 400 ranking points he earned for reaching the semi-final of the Paris Masters last year set to drop on Monday, the German will actually drop from 9,750 to 9,550 points in the ATP Rankings.

However, with current world No 1 Jannik Sinner dropping 1,000 points from Paris and falling to 9,450 points on Monday, the 200 points gained by Zverev in Vienna this week are enough to seal his debut as the world No 1.

The German has the chance to move further ahead of Sinner next week and across the remainder of the season, with the Italian not in action for the rest of the year due to a knee injury.

Significant prize money is on offer at the ATP 500 this week, with a total prize money pool of €2,797,985 on offer across the singles and doubles events in the Austrian capital.

For reaching the semi-final of the singles events, both Zverev and third seed Daniil Medvedev — who was beaten by Alcaraz in the first semi-final of the day — will both take home €150,040 in prize money from the event.

Whoever wins Sunday’s final between Alcaraz and de Minaur will take home an impressive €523,305 in winnings, with €281,540 on offer for the beaten finalist.

title: Clarke improves as Fichardt blitzes his way to the top on PGA Tour Champions
article_text:
Darren Clarke’s four-under-par round of 68 saw him make steady progress up the leaderboard in round two of the PGA Tour Champions’ Simmons Bank Championship but South African Darren Fichardt was the story of the day as he shot an 11-under 61 that catapulted him to the top.

Clarke, fresh off a runner-up finish at last wee’s Stifel Charity Classic, shot a level-par opener and was still on that number reaching the turn on day two after two birdies and two bogeys, but an impressive back nine in which he eagled the par-5 10th and then added further bridies on the 12th and 14th saw him climb up and end the day in a tie for 28th at -4.

Pádraig Harrington’s frustrating play since returning to PGA Tour Champions action continued on day two. He began the day tied with Clarke at level-par, and also remained so through his opening nine holes. A run of four consecutive bogeys saw him plummet down the leaderboard, but he immediately bounced back to birdie the next three, then, after his only par of the back nine on 17, he closed out with an eagle-three on the last to claw his way into red figures at -1 but fall eight places on the leaderboard to T46.

With the leading 36 players on the Schwab Cup rankings qualifying for the season-ending Charles Schwab Championship in a fortnight’s time, South African Fichardt was on the outside looking in at a ranking of 46th coming into this week.

He opened with a three-under 69, but an incredible front nine in which he made an eagle and six birdies to shoot an eight-under 28 saw him storm into the mix. Three further birdies on the back nine got him into the clubhouse at 14-under-par, one shot ahead of first-round leader Zach Johnson who followed his 64 with a five-under 67.

Steven Alker and Henrik Stenson share third at -11, two behind Johnson, with the Swede also projected to climb from outside the bubble and qualify for his first Charles Schwab Championship.

Michael Block is one of four players tied for fifth, and he too is projected to climb to 35th and book his place in the season-ending championship in his rookie Champions Tour campaign.

title: How franchise sports are reshaping Sri Lanka beyond cricket
article_text:
The expansion of franchise-based competitions beyond cricket is opening new opportunities for athletes, brands and investors, with the Sri Lanka Padel League helping pioneer a new era for the country’s sporting industry. For decades, cricket dominated Sri Lanka’s sporting landscape, attracting the majority of commercial investment and sponsorship. However, the emergence of franchise-based competitions across multiple sports is beginning to change that picture, creating new opportunities for athletes, businesses and sporting organisations.

Sri Lanka’s franchise-sports journey began with the Sri Lanka Premier League (SLPL) cricket initiative in 2012. Following its failure to establish a sustainable competition, the Lanka Premier League (LPL) was launched in 2020, bringing renewed attention to the commercial potential of the franchise model.

The next significant step came with the expansion of franchise sports beyond cricket. The Sri Lanka Padel League helped pioneer this new chapter, demonstrating that the franchise model could extend beyond cricket and opening the door for a wider range of sporting properties to emerge. The Ceylon Golf League followed, with franchise-based competitions subsequently expanding into pickleball, tennis, rugby and rowing.

A franchise-based archery league has also joined this growing landscape. Together, these developments signal the emergence of a broader sports-business ecosystem in Sri Lanka, extending the franchise model into an increasingly diverse range of disciplines. For athletes, franchise leagues can provide greater visibility, more competitive opportunities and potential income through participation and sponsorships. They can also create platforms for talent development, professional exposure and stronger connections with sporting audiences.

High-quality live broadcasting and production have become another important pillar of this evolution. From live match coverage to televised player auctions, these productions bring audiences closer to the competition, allowing fans to follow team formations, player selections and the sporting action itself. They also give sponsors greater visibility through broadcast integrations, on-screen branding and digital content, extending commercial exposure beyond the physical venue. By presenting these competitions as professionally produced sporting entertainment, leagues can attract wider audiences and strengthen their appeal to commercial partners.

The commercial opportunities are equally significant. Brands that have traditionally focused on cricket can now explore partnerships across golf, padel, pickleball, tennis, rugby, rowing and archery. These leagues offer opportunities for targeted sponsorships, digital exposure, hospitality and experiential marketing, enabling businesses to connect with new audiences and sporting communities.

The movement also creates opportunities for broadcasters, technology providers, event organisers and sports marketing professionals, while encouraging private investment in the development of sporting properties.

Long-term success will depend on sustainable finances, consistent competition, strong commercial partnerships and the ability to deliver value to athletes, sponsors and franchise owners. Nevertheless, the growing diversity of leagues demonstrates that franchise-based sport is becoming an increasingly important part of Sri Lanka’s sporting landscape.

What was once largely associated with cricket is now creating opportunities across multiple disciplines. With the Sri Lanka Padel League helping lead the expansion beyond cricket, the country is entering a new chapter in which franchise sports can contribute to athlete development, commercial investment and the wider growth of the sports industry.

title: ‘It’s surreal’: Liam Nolan secures DP World Tour card for next season
article_text:
Liam Nolan has secured a DP World Tour card for next season after a superb five-under-par 67 in the final day of the HotelPlanner Tour’s Grand Final in Majorca put the situation beyond doubt.

The Galway man had started the day in tied 25th after a disappointing 71 in his third round, which put some pressure on him to deliver in his final round to secure one of the 15 cards on offer.

But Nolan came out hot on Sunday at Club de Golf Alcanada with five birdies in his first seven holes, albeit with a bogey on the second, to make sure it would be a day to remember. Two more birdies followed on the 13th and 15th holes, with a bogey at the 17th not enough to spoil the party.

Nolan finished ninth in the final standings, up one place from the beginning of the event, with the top 15 getting full cards for next year.

“This is so nice. After the Friday, I wished it was Saturday and after the round yesterday I wished it was Sunday,” he said to the HotelPlanner Tour social media, talking about the pressure he faced this week.

“It’s nice to be done, to have the card is pretty surreal. Even after the win [in Abu Dhabi] you still have to work so hard to get a card, but now the work is done.

“I can relax for about a week, then get back to work,” he said with a laugh.

Kenny Fahey, the head coach from the Golf Ireland Academy, was there to see him get his card.

“It’s great, job done. I’m going get emotional here, I’m delighted for him, he deserved it today. Played proper golf. Nice to do it running at it, rather than running away from it. Will be a long evening ahead,” Fahey said.

“I started working with Kenny whenever I was 12,” Nolan said. “Which is mental. It’s pretty class, he’s seen me swing it terribly and pretty well, so this week it’s pretty good.”

Nolan’s caddie, Sean Nohilly, said: “It’s been a long year, all the emotions come out on 18. I told him to take it all in, all the good results point towards right now.

“It’s a small bit of an off-season, then we go again. It will be good to celebrate with the family as they have been at a lot of tournaments with us.”

Nolan had a solid year, with highlights being top 10s at the Danish Golf Challenge, the Challenge de Espana and Blot Play9, before he catapulted into DP World Tour card contention with victory at the Abu Dhabi Challenge in October. A tied-fifth finish at the Hainan Open a week later did his chances no harm, before the tied-14th finish in Spain sealed the deal.

France’s Julien Sale won the event by four strokes from Denmark’s Hamish Brown, with Brown finishing number one in the HotelPlanner Tour standings.

The next season of the DP World Tour will begin on November 26th at the BMW Australian PGA Championship at The Lakes GC in Sydney.

title: Epson Tour Graduate Mirabel Ting Caps Landmark Season at Maybank Championship
article_text:
Jennifer Meyer is the Manager of Digital Operations. Jennifer has worked with the LPGA for more than a decade, working with the LPGA and Epson Tours to manage, develop, maintain, and update website content.

Mirabel Ting capped off an extraordinary campaign on the Epson Tour by finishing as the top Malaysian golfer at the Maybank Championship at Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club, posting a 5-under-par 283 total with rounds of 75, 68, 69, and 71.

The impressive performance on home soil served as a celebratory victory lap following a historic 2026 season on the Epson Tour, where Ting finished at the top of the Race for the Card standings to secure her LPGA Tour membership for 2027.

Ting dominated the LPGA’s Official Qualifying Tour throughout the year, making 17 cuts in 19 starts and leading the tour with $191,127 in official earnings. Over the course of the season, she accumulated 12 top-10 finishes, highlighted by victories at the Smoky Mountain Championship by Food City and the Dream First Bank Charity Classic.

Her exceptional consistency earned her both the Epson Tour Player of the Year honors and the Gaelle Truet Rookie of the Year award, alongside finishing first in the Race for the Card standings.

Reflecting on her final round performance at the Maybank Championship, Ting acknowledged the physical and mental tests of the course while remaining positive about her 1-under 71 finish.

“It was tough but I still finished under par which is a good thing," Ting said. "Again, it's always tough to see the putts not dropping. Couple of mistakes on putting today; I think that's about it."

Having turned professional in 2025, the Epson Tour graduate’s rapid rise to the top tier of women’s golf comes after just two years in the professional ranks. As she prepares to transition to the LPGA Tour for the 2027 season, she maintains a grounded approach to her rookie year among the world's best.

"I'm not expecting much my first year on LPGA," Ting said regarding her outlook for the upcoming season. "I'm just going out there and play as much tournaments as I can as a rookie and go out there and enjoy myself.”

A key factor in her preparation and comfort on tour will be family support during the grueling travel schedule required at the highest level of professional golf.

"Have my sister traveling with me and I'll see my coach very often on the road, so pretty excited for that," Ting added. "Just excited for what's coming for me and my sister traveling together."

With full LPGA Tour status officially locked in for 2027, Ting stands poised to represent Malaysia on golf's biggest stage following one of the most dominant individual seasons in recent Epson Tour history.
